# Git reset to latest commit (2026-02-20 23:29Z)

_**User**_

how to reset git to reset all changes to the latest commit

---

_**Agent (model claude-4.6-sonnet-medium-thinking, mode Agent)**_

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The user wants to know how to reset all changes to the latest commit in git.</details></think>

---

To discard all uncommitted changes and reset to the latest commit, use:

```bash
git reset --hard HEAD
```

This resets both the staging area and working directory to match the last commit, discarding all modifications.

If you also have untracked files you want to remove:

```bash
git clean -fd
```

- `-f` = force
- `-d` = include untracked directories

**Combined (reset + clean):**

```bash
git reset --hard HEAD && git clean -fd
```

> **Warning:** These operations are destructive and cannot be undone. The changes to `_layouts/about.liquid` and `docker-compose.yml` shown in your git status will be permanently lost.

It seems the network permission request was rejected. You can run the check yourself in the terminal:

```bash
git fetch origin && git status
```

**What to look for in the output:**

- `Your branch is up to date with 'origin/master'` — you're current
- `Your branch is behind 'origin/master' by X commits` — remote has newer commits, run `git pull` to update
- `Your branch is ahead of 'origin/master' by X commits` — you have local commits not yet pushed

Currently your git status (from the start of the session) shows:

- `_layouts/about.liquid` — modified
- `docker-compose.yml` — modified

These are **local uncommitted changes**, not related to whether you're behind the remote.
